status: accepted after user reported successful tests; specific OS/provider coverage not separately enumerated
ownership: Weather in app/tools/services/weather.py; same instance/store from main to core/NativeBridge; model weather.locations/current through registry/policy/TaskManager; native dashboard polls the same cache without journal tasks

location.manual: Explicit selection among up to five labelled provider candidates; no implicit first match
location.auto: Only a user click and sharing confirmation request browser geolocation; rounded to two decimals before transfer/persistence
location.startup: Reuse approved saved place; never request geolocation automatically
location.preferences: weatherLocation in the existing native JsonStore, same lock and write/readback; generic UI save/import cannot grant consent
location.privacy: Coarse coordinates remain local preferences and provider request parameters, not model results/poll logs; city queries may remain in task history

provider.name: Open-Meteo, place data via GeoNames
provider.kind: modelled current conditions; not a local sensor or daily forecast
provider.units: Celsius, humidity percent, km/h; explicit UTC observation/fetch timestamps
provider.transport: fixed HTTPS URLs, no redirects/keys, connect/read timeouts, streaming budget and 64 KiB response limit; no automatic retries
provider.cache: 600 seconds fresh, 60-second failed-refresh backoff, at most 3600 seconds retained stale, 32 entries
provider.terms: default public endpoint is non-commercial; attribution links in UI/docs; no upstream server source imported

covered: no configured location means no provider request
same cache/real zero values across model and dashboard
ambiguous location search does not silently change a preference; actual candidate IDs required
invalid/missing/range/unit/time/provider data never becomes current success
failed refresh becomes stale, backs off, eventually clears, then recovers
coarse Auto storage, persistence/restart, Clear and generic-save consent isolation
Stop before provider calls, cancelled read completion and location-change stale-response rejection
invalid search/corrupt settings are failed read results, not a persistent unknown core lock
both real conversational SDK transports with synthetic provider responses and no note-consent dependency
public HTTP transport fixed endpoints, response limits, status/error redaction and invalid JSON handling
browser manual selection/XSS-safe labels, zero/stale/unavailable, no second save, no startup GPS
denied/hung browser location preserves manual fallback; late permission callback cannot save after timeout
real WebView2 selection -> persisted native location -> zero-valued weather rendering -> separate-process restoration
initial_failures_and_corrections: New weather dispatch pushed NativeBridge.event beyond Pyright complexity analysis. Only the cohesive weather dispatch was extracted into _weather_event; final app type check passed without suppression.
Initial weather browser test tried editing a field in a closed Settings modal; fixture now explicitly opens Settings/Connection.
Adding both provider credits made an unscoped credit selector match two links; browser assertion is now scoped to the weather widget.
A public-transport test initially called the autouse isolated weather helper instead of the native helper; it now retains the original request function while mocking only HTTP transport.
Datetime offset type narrowing was made explicit after Pyright reported an optional timedelta access.
Source validation was hardened to reject empty place labels and validate the full candidate before persistence; focused and full regression passed.
public_probe: weather-public-probe.json; successful fixed public London coordinate, not user geolocation
limits: User reported successful tests; specific OS/browser geolocation and provider coverage was not separately enumerated.
WeatherLocation is intentionally native-only and excluded from legacy UI JSON import/export; generic save/import cannot silently enable location sharing.
Provider current conditions are weather-model data. Unsupported/stale/missing responses are not local observations or tomorrow's forecast.
Previous persistent-unknown reconciliation and intermittent pythonnet/native-smoke complexity boundaries remain open; no claim they were fixed here.
No paid API, real user location, notes or account were used in automatic checks. Portable demo was not rebuilt.
commit: accepted weather work committed before subsequent UI cleanup
